A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LGS-Net and Latent Guided Sampling by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original TSP and CVRP benchmark results, inference-method comparisons, training curves, and particle-count and update-frequency analyses in Section 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains original routing results and reports additional component ablations, baseline comparisons, CVRP200 results, and knapsack experiments in Section 6 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The reported training prescription changes materially: Equation (2) switches from +βH to −βH, while Appendix A revises the decoder entropy-gradient sign, adds entropy contributions to the encoder estimator, and changes baseline placement. V2 also introduces a separately trained diffusion-prior variant and a knapsack decoder adaptation. The core encoder-decoder and interacting MCMC/SA framework remains; these documentary changes do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original routing coverage and adds CVRP200 evaluation in Table 11 and 0/1 Knapsack50 and Knapsack100 experiments in Table 13, extending empirical coverage beyond routing. CVRP with time windows and job shop scheduling are outlined in Appendix A.3 but are not experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 adds ELG and CNF to the corresponding TSP/CVRP comparisons, HGS to the CVRP comparison, and Adam and SGLD to the existing inference-method comparison. Table 9 additionally evaluates Active Search + IL and AGFN (greedy). These are reported comparisons absent from v1, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: Reported training duration changes from 2000 epochs in v1 Appendix E.1 to 8000 in v2 Appendix F.1; v1 Figure 4 already reached 8000, so this does not demonstrate additional training. POMO computational budgets/runtimes are revised, including CVRP100 without augmentation from 10 to 40 minutes. New experiments introduce controlled latent-dimension/radius settings, a diffusion-prior training protocol, and specified knapsack sample counts and capacities.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's inference-method, particle-count, and update-frequency analyses, v2 tests cost-weighted versus POPPY training, instance-conditioned versus independent priors, COMPASS + LGS, deterministic versus stochastic latents, and encoder versus diffusion priors. Tables 6–8, 10, and 12 and Figure 7 also examine latent dimension and radius. The earlier particle-count and update-frequency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 3 and v2 Figure 2 both report means over 10 inference runs, and the existing particle-count boxplots are retained. V2 does not introduce new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures for the expanded results.

E6.justification: The original LGS benchmark scores for TSP/CVRP100–150 remain unchanged, while POMO scores are revised alongside computational budgets. Numerous results are added: Table 7 reports CVRP100 objectives of 15.641 for the instance-independent model versus 15.524 for the conditioned model; Table 11 reports LGS's CVRP200 gap of 1.289%; Table 13 reports knapsack objectives of 20.018 and 40.512. These are new comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds an importance-sampling derivation, Proposition A.1 and its gradient proof, an inference-gradient derivation, and a conditional proposal-symmetry argument. It makes compactness explicit in the theoretical setting and replaces the exponential Lyapunov drift arguments with whole-state minorization and V=1 in Appendices C and D. Assumptions 4 and 8 and the associated Jensen step change from squared to unsquared L2 norms.

C1.justification: The central contributions—instance-conditioned latent modeling, interacting MCMC with SA, and convergence guarantees—remain. V2 broadens the headline performance claim from RL-based methods to NCO/learning-based baselines and adds an explicit contribution concerning effectiveness under low inference budgets.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of instance conditioning, stochastic latents, training-loss differences, gradient-computation costs, and the diffusion prior's additional training requirements. It substantially expands limitations concerning scaling, longer decoding horizons, and global constraints that masking cannot enforce. The augmented CVRP150 loss to EAS remains acknowledged in Appendix F.2.2, although the main text now makes a broader all-settings superiority claim.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents encoder soft-clipping, inference updates restricted to the decoder's final layer, explicit baseline functions, budget-selection procedures, and a common PyTorch evaluation implementation. It supplies diffusion-prior training and knapsack-generation details. Existing architecture settings and the code-access link are retained. Describing R=40 as both a radius and a diameter leaves that implementation detail unresolved.

R1.justification: The new Extensive Related Work appendix positions the method against reward-guided sampling, diffusion fine-tuning, GFlowNets, and large-scale NCO approaches. Other additions connect the training objective to IWAE and best-of-many objectives and discuss newer generalization and memory-enhanced solvers. This substantially expands research positioning beyond v1's NCO and MCMC discussion.

P1.justification: The seven-section main structure and much of the existing method and theory exposition are retained. V2 rewrites portions of the introduction and related work, expands explanatory passages, adds experiment subheadings, and reorganizes appendix subsections. The supplementary contents page is removed. These narrative edits accompany the larger scientific additions.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text. The separate routing tables become a combined main comparison without augmentation, with expanded full comparisons in Appendix Tables 4–5. Existing figures are relocated, resized, or restyled; the latent visualization and inference curves exchange numbering. Tables 6–13 and the radius-sensitivity Figure 7 are new displays.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's missing validation of central design choices through component ablations, broader baselines, and non-routing evaluation. Corrected entropy/gradient expressions and explicit applicability limits also improve technical clarity. These gains outweigh remaining defects: the main text overstates performance across all settings despite the retained EAS win in Table 5, and Appendix A.4's new importance-sampling justification does not consistently reconcile normalized ratios with the summed training weights.
